message.abstract: <jats:p>In alignment with carbon neutrality goals, high-precision long-term wind power forecasting is vital for power system scheduling. However, non-stationarity, noise, and underexploited physical relationships limit existing models, especially during critical conditions. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a Physics-informed Operating Condition Attention Model, Phy-OCA. (1) Phy-OCA employs a dual-branch architecture to decouple input variables into an Energy branch (wind speed and historical power) and an Efficiency branch (wind direction) based on the aerodynamic power conversion mechanism. (2) An Operating Condition Attention module is introduced to evaluate temporal patches via physical indicators, guiding the encoder (centered around scalar Long ShortTerm Memory units) to prioritize critical intervals, such as power ramps and stochastic fluctuations. (3) Wind Speed-Direction Coupling mechanism is developed to characterize how wind directional shifts affect the wind speed capture efficiency of turbines. (4) The study constructs a spatiotemporal dataset comprising 132 real-world wind turbines in Northwest China. Experimental results demonstrate that Phy-OCA outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant accuracy improvements under critical conditions. This research offers a high-precision, interpretable solution for practical wind power forecasting.</jats:p>
title: A Physics-informed Operating Condition Attention Model for Wind Power Forecasting
